newsitem.title: UK: London palladium fixed at $150.00, 18-month high.
newsitem.headline: London palladium fixed at $150.00, 18-month high.

text.p: The price of the rare precious metal palladium was fixed at $150.00 per ounce on Wednesday, its highest fixing since August 22, 1995. Its sister metal platinum was fixed at $383.50, its highest since November 21 last year.
Dealers said world shortages of palladium, over 60 percent of which come from Russia's Norilsk mining and metallurgical combine in Arctic Seberia, have sent the price soaring this year.
A union official at the giant operation said a strike over pay arrears owed to workers could close the plant on March 15.
However a spokesman for Norilsk management later said this was unlikely.
Palladium is used in electronics, dentistry and in autocatalysts which remove toxic gases from car exhaust fumes. The largest user of the metal is Japan which accounts for 40 percent of world demand.
A background factor in addition to the Norilsk problems is a delayed start to Russia's 1997 supply contract negotiations with Japan which has stopped exports since late last year.
